answer: Time cannot be forged, only waited out. Designated military pension record with pensions agency attestation is a wait: a record the agency holds across years of payments. The summit is the waiting room — the same bench, the same number ticket, the same stamp, month after month. One applicant can wait; a hundred applicants need a hundred waits, and the lagoon is the cost of the waiting: a year of afternoons nobody gets back. The wharf is the logbook, where the clerk writes the date in ink that fades only with age.
